lessons.title: What Moves Gold Prices: The Dollar, Real Yields, Central Banks and the Rupee

children.text: Gold does not have earnings, a management team or a dividend policy. So why did it fall about 28% in dollar terms in 2013, and then nearly double from its 2015 low to break $2,000 an ounce in 2020, and keep climbing past $3,000 and $4,000 in 2025? The answer is a small set of forces that you can learn to read. By the end of this lesson you will understand the four big global drivers of gold (the US dollar, real interest rates, central bank buying and fear), plus the India-specific layers that decide what you actually pay on MCX or at a jeweller: the rupee, import duty and local demand.

body.text: Gold is priced globally in dollars, so most of its big moves are about the dollar, real interest rates and who is buying. What an Indian investor pays is that global price translated through the rupee, import duty and local demand.

children.text: Who Buys Gold, and Why It Matters
Gold demand comes from four very different buyers, each responding to different signals.

body.title: Approximate global gold demand by category, 2024 (tonnes, World Gold Council data, rounded)

children.text: Jewellery
is price-sensitive: when gold spikes, Indian and Chinese buyers often delay purchases or buy lighter pieces.
Investment demand
responds to interest rates, fear and momentum, and can swing sharply through ETF flows.
Central banks
buy for reserve diversification and are largely indifferent to short-term price moves.
Technology
is a small, stable slice, used in electronics.
Driver 1: The US Dollar

markDefs.definition: An index, often called DXY, measuring the US dollar against a basket of major currencies such as the euro, yen and pound.

children.text: Gold is quoted in US dollars per troy ounce, through benchmarks such as the LBMA Gold Price in London and COMEX futures in New York. When the dollar strengthens, gold becomes more expensive for buyers using other currencies, which tends to reduce demand. When the dollar weakens, the reverse happens. Traders often track the
US Dollar Index
, and gold has historically tended to move opposite to it.

body.text: The inverse link between gold and the dollar is a tendency, not a law. In moments of global panic, both can rise together, because investors rush into both as safe havens.

children.text: Driver 2: Real Interest Rates

markDefs.definition: An interest rate after subtracting expected inflation. For gold, traders often watch the yield on 10-year US Treasury Inflation-Protected Securities (TIPS).

children.text: Gold pays no interest. So the real question for a large investor is: what am I giving up to hold it? The answer is the
real yield
on safe government bonds.

body.caption: If a 10-year US Treasury yields 4.3% and expected inflation is 2.4%, the real yield is about 1.9%.

children.text: Falling real yields are usually good for gold.
Holding a non-yielding asset costs less when bonds pay little after inflation.
Rising real yields are usually bad for gold.
Safe bonds start paying a real return, and gold looks expensive to hold.

2013 is the classic example. As the US Federal Reserve signalled it would slow its bond buying, real yields jumped and gold fell about 28% in the calendar year, its worst year in decades. In 2020, real yields collapsed below zero as rates were cut to near zero during COVID, and gold set a record above $2,000.

body.text: Relationships shift. From 2022 onwards, US real yields rose sharply, which should have pushed gold down. Instead gold went on to record highs, largely because of record central bank buying. No single driver explains gold at all times, so weigh them together.

body.title: The opportunity cost
body.textWithBlank: Because gold pays no interest, it tends to do well when ___ yields, meaning bond yields after inflation, are falling.
body.explanation: Real yields measure what safe bonds pay after inflation. The lower they are, the less an investor gives up by holding gold instead.

children.text: Driver 3: Central Banks

Central banks hold gold as part of their foreign exchange reserves. For years they were modest buyers. That changed dramatically after 2022, when Western sanctions froze a large part of Russia's central bank reserves. Many central banks concluded that gold held in their own vaults is a reserve that no foreign government can freeze.

children.text: The RBI has been one of the steadier buyers, alongside central banks such as those of China, Poland and Turkey. Because these buyers are large and not very price-sensitive, their demand can put a floor under gold even when other drivers, like real yields, point the other way.
Driver 4: Fear and Uncertainty

markDefs.definition: An asset investors buy during market stress or crises because they expect it to hold value when other assets fall.

children.text: Gold is the classic
safe haven

. Wars, banking crises, sovereign debt scares and sharp equity sell-offs tend to send investors towards it. These moves can be fast and can fade quickly once the panic passes, so they matter most to short-term traders.

children.text: The India Layer: From Global Price to Your Price
The four drivers set the global dollar price. An Indian buyer then faces three more layers.
The rupee.
The dollar price is converted at USD/INR. A weaker rupee lifts Indian gold prices even if global gold is flat, as you saw in Chapter 1.
Import duty.
India imports almost all its gold, and customs duty is added to the landed price. MCX gold prices include duty, which is why they sit above the simple conversion of the international price.
GST and local premium.
GST of 3% applies when you buy physical gold. On top of that, local dealers may charge a premium or offer a discount depending on demand.

body.caption: A simplified landed-cost formula. In practice, duty is levied on a notified tariff value and local premiums or discounts also apply. MCX futures prices exclude GST.

body.title: Build the landed price
body.prompt: International gold is $2,500 per troy ounce, USD/INR is 84, and import duty is 6%. Using the simplified formula, what is the Indian price per 10 grams including duty but before GST, to the nearest rupee?
body.explanation: $2,500 ÷ 31.1035 × 10 = $803.77 per 10 grams. × 84 = about ₹67,517. × 1.06 for duty = about ₹71,568. Adding 3% GST would take a physical purchase to about ₹73,715.

body.title: Show me the math: what the July 2024 duty cut did

children.text: In the Union Budget of July 2024, the government cut the total customs duty on gold from 15% to 6%. Using the same base of about ₹67,517 per 10 grams before duty:
Difference: about ₹6,076 per 10 grams, a fall of about 7.8%

Nothing changed in global gold, the dollar or central bank demand, yet the Indian price dropped sharply because of a policy decision. Domestic gold prices and MCX gold fell steeply on Budget day. Duty rates can change again in any Budget, so always check the current rate.
Seasonal Demand in India

Indian buying peaks around Akshaya Tritiya, Dhanteras and Diwali, and the wedding season. Seasonal demand has a real effect on local premiums and import volumes, but India alone rarely moves the global dollar price in a big way. When global prices spike, Indian demand often softens and local dealers can even quote discounts to the landed price.

body.title: Read the combination
body.question: Which combination is most likely to push MCX gold prices higher?
options: The Fed signals more rate hikes, and the rupee strengthens
US real yields fall, and the rupee weakens against the dollar
The Union Budget cuts import duty on gold, and the dollar strengthens
Global equities rally strongly, and central banks pause gold buying
body.explanation: Falling real yields support the global dollar price of gold, and a weaker rupee raises the rupee price on top of that. The other options each include at least one force pushing Indian gold prices down.

body.title: Read the morning headlines
body.scenario:
Sameer, a 45-year-old CA in Ahmedabad who holds some gold ETFs, reads four headlines one morning:
1. "US inflation cools faster than expected; markets price in Fed rate cuts."
2. "Dollar index slides to a multi-month low."
3. "World Gold Council: central banks keep adding gold."
4. "Rupee strengthens sharply on strong foreign inflows."
body.prompt: For each headline, say whether it is likely to push the rupee price of gold up or down, and give your overall read.
body.modelAnswer:
1. Cooling US inflation and expected rate cuts: likely lower nominal yields, and usually lower real yields. Supportive for gold.
2. Weaker dollar index: supportive for the dollar price of gold.
3. Continued central bank buying: supportive, and a steady source of demand.
4. Stronger rupee: negative for the rupee price of gold, because each dollar of gold converts into fewer rupees.

Overall: three drivers push the global dollar price up, while the stronger rupee offsets part of the gain for Indian investors. Sameer should expect Indian gold to rise less than international gold, in percentage terms, on a day like this. The key habit is to separate the global dollar move from the rupee move rather than reacting to a single headline.

cards.definition: The global benchmark price for gold in US dollars per troy ounce, set in London.
A measure of the dollar against major currencies; gold tends to move opposite to it.
Bond yield minus expected inflation; falling real yields tend to support gold.
An asset bought during crises because it is expected to hold value.
Official purchases for reserves, above 1,000 tonnes a year in 2022 to 2024.
International price converted to rupees plus import duty, before GST and local premiums.
Total customs duty on gold cut from 15% to 6%, lowering Indian prices overnight.

points: Gold demand comes from jewellery, investment, central banks and technology, and each responds to different signals.
A weaker US dollar and falling real yields usually support gold; a stronger dollar and rising real yields usually weigh on it.
Central bank buying above 1,000 tonnes a year from 2022 to 2024 helped gold rise even as real yields climbed.
Fear drives sharp but often short-lived rallies.
Indian prices add three layers: USD/INR, import duty and GST, plus local premiums or discounts.
Policy matters: the July 2024 duty cut from 15% to 6% lowered Indian gold prices by about 7.8% in theory, with no change in global gold.
